To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the primary sources of Salmonella in turkeys are feed and litter, and that the primary means of transmission are horizontal, via the air, feed, litter, and drinkers.
Salmonella was isolated at a high frequency from litter, drinker and feeder contents, and air, and was also present in feed shipments.

Salmonella colonization of turkeys and the spread of the pathogen within the production environment were extensive once initial contamination occurred, and that drinker, feeders, and litter were critical sources of Salmonella transmission within and between pens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ecology of the Salmonella in a turkey facility.
Salmonella contamination of turkey production facilities.
the ecology of Salmonella in a newly constructed turkey facility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Salmonella colonization was extensive and horizontal transmission was common once initial contamination occurred.

Salmonella was introduced into the production facility prior to placement of turkeys and that horizontal transmission of Salmonella was extensive within each pen as evidenced by the presence of Salmonellae in drinkers, litter, feeders, and air.
Salmonella was present in the environment of both flocks and was transmitted horizontally from pen to pen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the primary sources of Salmonella contamination were the feed and the environment.
Salmonella is present throughout the turkey production system.
Salmonella was present in 2 of 6 feed shipments, in all litter and air samples, and in all drinker samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Salmonella is ubiquitous in the environment and that the best way to prevent salmonella colonization is to prevent initial contamination of the house.
Salmonella is present in the environment of a turkey production facility and that it spreads horizontally between pens and vertically to the birds.
it’s very important to control Salmonella in the environment.
